text_blocks.snippet: At-home COVID tests are generally accurate when used as directed, particularly when individuals are symptomatic. Positive results are usually reliable, but negative results, especially in the absence of symptoms, may be less accurate and should be followed up with repeat testing.
snippet_highlighted_words: generally accurate when used as directed, particularly when individuals are symptomatic

list.title: Symptomatic Individuals:
list.snippet: Studies indicate that at-home antigen tests are quite accurate in detecting COVID-19 when individuals are experiencing symptoms.

list.title: Asymptomatic Individuals:
list.snippet: At-home tests may be less sensitive in detecting the virus when someone does not have symptoms.

list.title: Negative Results:
list.snippet: A negative result, especially in the absence of symptoms, should be followed up with repeat testing to minimize the risk of a false negative.

list.title: Positive Results:
list.snippet: Positive results from at-home tests are generally reliable and indicate the presence of the virus.

list.title: Type of Test:
list.snippet: It's important to note that at-home tests are typically antigen tests, which are not as sensitive as molecular tests (like PCR).
Follow the instructions on the test kit carefully.
Repeat testing is recommended after a negative result, especially if symptoms are present.
If you have concerns about a test result or have symptoms, consult with a healthcare professional.
Voluntarily report your test results (positive or negative) to help track the spread of the virus, according to the FDA.
